title: Mission 3 — The Riddle King (Challenge B: The Pun Boss)
brief: The Riddle King guards the next clue, and he only speaks in riddles and puns. A word-for-word translation would make him boring, or his riddle impossible to solve. Recreate his wordplay in English so that the riddle can still be solved and the jokes still land.
teaching_objectives: Tell a pun that can be translated from one that has to be recreated.
Handle linked strings: a riddle, its answer and the reaction must change together.
Brief an AI translator to prioritise effect (solvable, funny) over literal meaning, and compare several creative solutions.
Handle a culture-specific genre (猜燈謎, lantern riddles) for international players.
scene_context: Kwai Heung Street lantern fair. 猜燈謎 (guessing lantern riddles) is a real Mid-Autumn and Lantern Festival tradition: riddles hang from lanterns and whoever guesses right wins a small prize. The Riddle King, a retired teacher, runs the riddle stall and knows where the rabbit lantern is. He challenges the player with a character riddle; the right answer earns a clue, the wrong one earns a roasting.

characters.profile: A retired schoolteacher in a tall hat and a long beard who runs the riddle stall at every lantern fair. Nobody on the street remembers his real name.
characters.voice: Theatrical, pompous and very pleased with himself. Speaks in rhymes, homophone puns and character riddles, with mock-classical phrasing. Roasts wrong answers mercilessly but good-naturedly.
characters.relationships: Knows everyone on the street and knows where the lantern is, but only hands out clues as prizes.

glossary.note: A festival tradition. Keep the word 'riddle'.
Character name shown in the speaker tag.
Traditional Chinese decorative archway at the entrance to the street.
Classic Hong Kong mooncake filling with two salted egg yolks.
Invented street name in an old Kowloon neighbourhood. Use this romanisation in every mission; do not translate it as 'Osmanthus Street'.

strings.source: {player_name}，想知道兔燈的下落？先過我這關！猜中有賞；猜錯嘛……我就「月」笑「月」大聲！
strings.speaker: riddle_king
strings.context: At the lantern-riddle (猜燈謎) stall of the fair, a man in a tall hat and a long beard blocks the player's way: the Riddle King. He addresses the player by name.
strings.intended_meaning: He addresses the player by name, says he knows about the rabbit lantern, and sets the terms: get past his challenge first; a right guess wins a prize. The threat is a pun: the set pattern 越笑越大聲 ('the more..., the louder I laugh') is written with 月 (moon) in place of its exact homophone 越 (Cantonese jyut6, Mandarin yuè), and the quotation marks flag the swap. Tone: theatrical, gloating.
constraints: Keep {player_name}
Recreate a moon pun (or another festival pun) in English
Theatrical, boastful tone

strings.source: 聽好了：「小白兔，愛玩耍，丟了尾巴也不怕。」——打一字！
strings.speaker: riddle_king
strings.context: The Riddle King poses a character riddle (字謎). 打一字 is the formula that tells the player the answer is a single written character.
strings.intended_meaning: A short rhyming verse (耍 / 怕 rhyme in both Cantonese and Mandarin): 'a little white rabbit loves to play; it loses its tail and isn't bothered'. 打一字 = 'the answer is one character'. The answer is 免: the character 兔 (rabbit) minus its final dot 丶 (the 'tail') is 免. Double clue: 免 also means 'spared / no need', echoing 也不怕 ('no need to worry'). The pun is visual, so it works whatever dialect the reader speaks.
constraints: The riddle must be solvable in English, so the English answer will be a different word
Keep the idea of a rabbit losing its tail
Keep a riddle formula at the end (the English equivalent of 打一字)
The riddle, the correct answer button and Ending A must be translated together

strings.source: 是「免」字！兔子沒了尾巴嘛！
strings.context: Choice button 1 of 2: the correct answer to the character riddle, with the player's reasoning.
strings.intended_meaning: The correct answer: 'It's the character 免! The rabbit (兔) lost its tail (the final dot).' 嘛 adds 'obviously!'. In English the button must name whatever word the English riddle points to.
constraints: Maximum 50 characters
Must give the answer to the English riddle
Should show the 'rabbit without its tail' logic
Single line

strings.context: Choice button 2 of 2: the wrong answer from a hungry detective who was not listening.
strings.intended_meaning: A blurted wrong answer: 'Mooncake! It must be mooncake!' It is not even a character, which is the joke. It sets up the roast in Ending B.
constraints: Maximum 50 characters
Single line

strings.source: 燈謎大王撫鬚大笑：「妙！兔子沒了尾巴，就是『免』——這條線索就免費送你：要找燈，就得『等』。月亮爬上牌坊頂，兔子自然現身。」
strings.context: Ending A: the player solves the riddle and is rewarded with a clue, which is itself a pun.
strings.intended_meaning: He strokes his beard, laughs, and praises the answer (妙 'brilliant'). Two jokes: (1) the answer 免 leads into 免費 'free of charge', so the clue is given 'for free'; (2) the clue: to find the lantern (燈), you must wait (等). 燈 (lantern) and 等 (wait) are a NEAR-homophone, not an exact one: Cantonese dang1 / dang2, Mandarin dēng / děng (same syllable, different tone). Literal content of the clue: once the moon has risen as high as the top of the archway (牌坊), the rabbit shows up of its own accord.
constraints: The first joke must follow from the English answer chosen for the riddle
Recreate a lantern / light / waiting pun
Nested quotation marks 『』 inside 「」 must become English double and single quotation marks (plain text only, no italics)
Single paragraph

strings.source: 燈謎大王笑彎了腰：「月餅？你餓到腦袋都變蓮蓉了！雙黃蓮蓉，兩隻蛋——正好是你的分數！」
strings.context: Ending B: wrong answer; the player gets comically roasted.
strings.intended_meaning: He doubles over laughing: the player is so hungry their brain has turned into lotus paste (蓮蓉, mooncake filling). Punchline: a double-yolk mooncake has two eggs, and 'getting an egg' (零蛋 / 鴨蛋) means scoring zero, so two eggs is exactly the player's score. Good-natured mockery.
constraints: Recreate the 'egg = zero' joke or find an equivalent roast
Good-natured, not insulting
Single paragraph
